content: Photorealistic CGI product photography shot from directly overhead — camera pointed straight down at a 90-degree vertical angle, flat lay composition, true bird's-eye top-down perspective. The product lies completely flat and horizontal on the surface below, photographed from directly above. Studio Digital S35, Premium Modern Prime lens, 35mm focal length, f/4 aperture, 16:9 aspect ratio. Scene: the product rests centered on a clean surface, bathed in dramatic caustic light patterns projected downward from above — refracted amber light rays scatter and dance across both the product surface and the surrounding scene, casting deep rich amber pools and sharp high-contrast shadow forms across the composition. The caustic light is the visual protagonist: striking, bold, optically refracted amber beams break across the product and the surface in sharp geometric patterns — warm deep amber, burnt gold, and near-translucent honey tones alternate with dense shadow pockets. Lighting: primary light source from directly above the scene, generating strong caustic refraction effects — amber-dominant color grade, warm golden backlighting filtered through a refractive element, hard-edged caustic patterns with sharp falloff into deep cool shadow zones. The contrast between the glowing amber caustics and the dense surrounding shadows is extreme and intentional. The product surface catches the caustic highlights with tack-sharp specular precision — no blur, no softness, ultra sharp focus across the entire product face. Shadows are deep, dimensional and purposeful, framing the product geometry against the ambient darkness. Style: luxury editorial product photography, high-drama architectural lighting study, premium commercial beauty render. Constraints: no splash, no liquid, no people, no text, no watermark, no extra logos, no eye-level angle, no angled perspective — strictly overhead 90-degree top-down.

A weathered farm worker sits on a worn wooden bench positioned just outside the front of a rustic cottage on a working coffee farm, leaning forward with focused intent as he pulls on a heavy leather boot, one foot already booted planted firmly on the ground.
The camera is positioned at a 3/4 front angle, slightly to the right of the subject, capturing both the front plane of his body and the side profile of his face in a naturally balanced, three-dimensional composition that reads as deeply photographic and cinematically grounded.
His calloused hands grip the boot heel with practiced ease, the quiet ritual of a man who has done this a thousand mornings before.
He pauses mid-motion, gaze lifting toward the sprawling farm ahead — a private moment of stillness before the labor begins.
The human figure is anatomically precise and photorealistic: correct hand anatomy with exactly five fingers per hand, natural skin pores, realistic knuckle detail, accurate boot construction with visible stitching and sole edge, natural weight distribution in seated posture, believable fabric wrinkle physics on worn denim and cotton shirt, no floating limbs, no merged surfaces, no distorted joints.

The 3/4 front framing places him slightly left of center, his body turned at approximately 45 degrees toward camera, revealing the full texture of his worn cotton shirt across the chest and shoulder while his boot-pulling gesture reads clearly in natural perspective.
The farm landscape unfolds in soft cinematic depth behind him.
Vast rows of coffee plantations stretch across rolling hills, the dark green leaves of the coffee trees catching the first fragile light of dawn, cherries of deep red and orange glinting faintly through the foliage.
In the mid-distance, large mechanical coffee harvesters sit positioned between the rows, their silhouettes emerging slowly from the pre-dawn mist — engines cold, waiting.
A second harvesting machine is visible further back, a worker in the cab preparing for the day's run.
All background elements are spatially coherent with correct perspective recession, no floating objects, no mirrored geometry, no repeated texture tiling errors, machinery proportions consistent with real harvesting equipment.

Dawn light breaks low and golden across the horizon, casting long amber rays that skim the tops of the coffee rows and paint the cottage facade in warm ochre tones.
The 3/4 front angle allows the dawn light to rake naturally across the near side of his face and chest, creating a convincing three-dimensional form with soft shadow falloff across his far cheek and shoulder.
A thin morning mist drifts across the lower fields, softening the background into layered planes of teal and olive shadow broken by shafts of golden backlight.
The shallow depth of field at f/4 keeps the farm worker razor-sharp — the cracked leather of his boot, the texture of his worn denim, the roughness of his sun-darkened hands — while the plantation and machinery dissolve into a beautifully rendered, emotionally resonant bokeh of green and gold.
Lighting is physically accurate with correct shadow direction unified across all scene elements, no inconsistent multiple light sources, no light bleeding through solid surfaces.

The cottage behind him shows peeling whitewash paint, a weathered wooden door left slightly ajar, a tin roof catching the first pink blush of the sky.
A tin coffee mug sits on the bench beside him, still steaming.
The ground around his boots is damp red earth, dark with morning dew.
Natural ambient dawn light, no artificial fill, volumetric rays filtering through the tree line at the field's edge.
Rich film grain texture, organic color gradation in shades of teal, amber, and deep earth tones.
